_comment: Raw IR metadata pulled from the dev host's /models/ov/ on 2026-08-28 (pre-M0 handover). sha256 prefixes, 16 hex chars. All three share tokenizer 87a7830d63fcf43b. full_attention_interval 4 = 1 in 4 layers full attention, rest GDN. Coder is expert-PRUNED: 184 of 256. 2026-08-28: mtp fields added after inspecting the IRs — all three checkpoints declare mtp_num_hidden_layers 1, and NONE of the exports contain an MTP graph (only 'logits'), so no MTP head is servable from these artifacts. 2026-08-28 (later): qwen38-b7c1-ov now DOES carry a servable MTP head. optimum-intel still drops it, so tools/export_mtp.py reconstructs it from the unquantised mtp.* tensors in /models/gptq/qwen38-gptq-mtp and writes openvino_mtp_layer.xml and openvino_mtp_lm_head.xml beside the model; measured 66% draft acceptance. The other two exports are unchanged.

qwen38-b7c1-ov.status: provisional, 7/10 (AWQ-only; SE calibration degenerates greedy - do not re-add SE)

qwen38-intel-int4-ov.status: 10/10 greedy on the acceptance task (paged+MTP, B60, 2026-08-30), 36.3 t/s, 90.8% draft acceptance (296/326); Intel's public int4 export with the reconstructed MTP head beside it; --mtp off 25.0 t/s, reconstructed layer 36.9-37.3 (code) / 33.8-34.0 (prose), Intel's exported layer + our lm_head 37.7-38.1 / 34.3-34.9 t/s
qwen38-intel-int4-ov._note: Intel's export also ships openvino_mtp_model.{xml,bin} of its own (263 MB int4, one MTP layer, no lm_head, same interface as our openvino_mtp_layer). arcint keys the head on openvino_mtp_layer + openvino_mtp_lm_head, which are the reconstructed ones.

qwen36-35b-a3b-mtp-ov.status: head pairs (93.9% code / 75.4% prose draft acceptance, B60, 2026-08-30); --mtp on 48-53 t/s vs 71.5 t/s off — the M=2 MoE forward runs the prefill path and the f16 dense-all-experts head costs 11 ms a draft; not for production
